**Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)** is the practice of creating and structuring content so that AI-powered systems are more likely to **find, understand, trust, and cite** it when generating answers. Instead of optimizing for a high position in traditional search results, GEO aims to increase the chances that your content is incorporated into AI-generated responses. [geodocs.dev](https://geodocs.dev/geo/what-is-geo?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### How GEO differs from SEO

Although GEO builds on many SEO principles, they have different goals:

| SEO | GEO |
|------|------|
| Optimizes for search engine rankings | Optimizes for inclusion in AI-generated answers |
| Success is measured by rankings and clicks | Success is measured by citations, mentions, and recommendations in AI responses |
| Focuses on keywords, backlinks, and technical SEO | Focuses on clarity, authority, structured information, and answer-ready content |


In practice, strong SEO often supports GEO, but it doesn't guarantee that AI systems will use your content. [geodocs.dev](https://geodocs.dev/geo/what-is-geo?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### Why GEO has become important

More people are asking questions directly to AI assistants rather than clicking through multiple search results. AI systems typically:

- Retrieve information from multiple sources.
- Compare and synthesize those sources.
- Generate a direct answer.
- Sometimes cite or link to the sources they used.

Businesses and publishers therefore want their content to be among the sources AI systems consider authoritative enough to reference. [geodocs.dev](https://geodocs.dev/geo/what-is-geo?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What makes content GEO-friendly?

While no one can guarantee that an AI system will cite a page, practices commonly associated with GEO include:

- Writing clear, direct answers to common questions.
- Organizing content with descriptive headings.
- Supporting factual claims with reliable sources.
- Demonstrating expertise and topical depth.
- Keeping information accurate and up to date.
- Using structured data where appropriate.
- Building a consistent, trustworthy presence across the web, not just on your own website. [geodocs.dev](https://geodocs.dev/geo/what-is-geo?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### Is GEO a separate discipline?

The term was introduced in a 2023 academic paper, which explored methods for improving the visibility of content in generative search systems and showed that certain optimization strategies could significantly increase how often content appeared in AI-generated responses. Since then, the concept has been widely adopted in digital marketing. [geodocs.dev](https://geodocs.dev/geo/what-is-geo?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### An example

Suppose someone asks an AI assistant:

> "What's the best way to reduce household energy bills?"

A traditional SEO strategy aims to have your article rank on the first page of search results.

A GEO strategy aims to have the AI assistant summarize your advice and cite your guide as one of the sources used to answer the question.

### Looking ahead

GEO is still evolving because AI systems differ in how they retrieve information, evaluate sources, and generate answers. Rather than replacing SEO, it's generally viewed as an additional layer of optimization for an AI-assisted search landscape. The most durable approach is to publish accurate, well-structured, authoritative content that is useful to people first—and readily understandable by AI systems second.
